# Consume neo-agent-skills 0.1.3 — the decision-sweep and ownership-disposition rules

## Context

`neo-agent-skills@0.1.3` published 2026-09-01, carrying `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#33` (resolves `#32` + `#34`). Two governance rules land with it, and both change what an agent does *before* `create_issue`:

- **`ticket-create` §1a gains two sweep arms.** The three existing arms are all *artifact* substrates — they answer *"does a ticket exist?"* and never *"was this already decided, and why?"* A `NOT_PLANNED` predecessor is a **ruling**, and an artifact sweep surfaces its title but never its reason. Arm `(iii)` is a Memory Core rationale query; arm `(iv)` is an own-assignment sweep read by **bodies, not titles**. Both attest in the ticket body.
- **`ticket-create` §10 gains an exhaustive ownership disposition.** Its assignment bullet gated on *"if you intend to start working immediately"*, so a ticket filed as a **finding** never satisfied the antecedent and orphaning it violated nothing. 84 of 164 open `neomjs/neo` issues carried no assignee. Unowned stays allowed; *silently* unowned does not.

## The Problem

This repository declares `neo-agent-skills: ^0.1.1` and its lockfile resolves **0.1.1**.

The manifest range is not the binding constraint — `^0.1.1` already admits `0.1.3` under npm's `0.x` caret semantics. **The lockfile is**, and it pins the old tarball. So every install here reproduces the pre-`#33` skill corpus, and the projected `.claude/skills` tree serves the rules without the two new arms. Nothing errors: the skills materialize, the guard passes, and the agent reads a `ticket-create` that is quietly one version behind the one the swarm agreed on.

That is the same failure shape the substrate keeps producing — a green install over a stale source. The corpus is *governance* substrate, so a stale resolution does not degrade a feature, it degrades the rules agents file work against.

## The Architectural Reality

- `package.json` declares the range; `package-lock.json` decides the bytes. A range bump without a lock refresh changes nothing, and a lock refresh without a range bump leaves the floor at a version that no longer carries the rules.
- Skills arrive as an npm dependency and are projected into `.claude/skills` as symlinks by the package's own postinstall linker (`neo-agent-skills-materialize`). **No skill bytes are committed here**, so there is no tree to diff — the only question worth asking is whether the projection happened, which is exactly what the `substrate-sync` workflow asserts via `--check`.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts` skips both `postinstall` and `prepare`, yielding a resolved dependency and zero reachable skills. Dependency resolution is not the same as skills being reachable.

## The Fix

Raise the declared floor to `^0.1.3` **and** refresh the lockfile in the same commit, so the version that carries the rules is both permitted and resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `package.json` declares `neo-agent-skills: ^0.1.3`.
- [ ] `package-lock.json` resolves `0.1.3` — verified by the `resolved` tarball URL, not by the range.
- [ ] `npx --no-install neo-agent-skills-materialize --check` passes at the new version, so the projection is proven reachable rather than merely resolved (the `substrate-sync` assertion).
- [ ] `.claude/skills` remains git-ignored — projection artifacts, never committed bytes.
- [ ] The materialized `ticket-create` payload carries the `(iii)`/`(iv)` sweep arms and §10's ownership disposition; a `grep` of the projected file is the honest instrument, since the version number alone does not prove the content arrived.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the skill payloads themselves — they are authored in `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` and consumed here.
- The sibling bumps in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` and `neomjs/neo-agent-institution`; each carries its own ticket because each has its own lockfile and CI.
- Auditing existing unassigned tickets against the new §10 rule. The rule governs creation from now on; a retroactive sweep of the 84 is separate work with its own evidence.

## Avoided Traps

- **Bumping only the range.** `^0.1.1` already admitted `0.1.3`; leaving the lock untouched means the install is unchanged and the ticket closes over nothing.
- **Bumping only the lock.** The floor would still permit a resolution without the rules, so a future `npm install` on a clean checkout could legitimately regress.
- **Reading the version number as proof of content.** The consumer-visible artifact is the projected payload, not the manifest — verify the rules are present in the materialized file.
- **Hand-editing `package-lock.json`.** Integrity hashes and the dependency graph belong to npm; the lock is regenerated, never authored.
